question: The Commission’s staff working document evaluating the Tobacco Products Directive (SWD(2026)0111) states that the evaluation ‘draws on a broad and diverse evidence base, including a supporting study conducted by an external contractor’.

A review of the SWD reveals that the 2025 study conducted by Open Evidence entitled ‘Study supporting the Evaluation of the Tobacco Control Acquis’ is referenced throughout the document, including in footnotes 92, 143, 148, 212, 221, 250 and 262, among others. Given the frequency and nature of these references, the study appears to constitute one of the primary evidentiary pillars of the evaluation.

However, the study did not appear to be publicly available immediately after the publication of the SWD’s conclusions. Meaningful scrutiny of the SWD’s conclusions necessarily requires immediate and easy access to the evidence on which those conclusions rest. The unavailability of this study has significantly impacted the ability to assess the robustness, completeness and objectivity of the evaluation. 1.
Can the Commission provide an explanation for the delay in the immediate release of Open Evidence’s supporting study, and confirm that it is now fully accessible?

Does the Commission consider this procedure consistent with its Better Regulation commitments and transparency obligations, given that an evaluation of the SWD relies heavily on an external study that was not made publicly available at the same time of the publication of the conclusions?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (3.9.2026) The evaluation1 of the Tobacco Products Directive2 and the Tobacco Advertising Directive3 was carried out in full compliance with the better regulation framework.

The data sources, methodologies, and analytical approaches underpinning the evaluation are described in the accompanying Commission Staff Working Document and its Annexes4, ensuring transparency regarding the evidence used.

Following the publication of the Staff Working Document, the Commission also published all supporting documents that were not yet publicly accessible at the time of its publication, including the external study referred to in the question. These documents are now fully accessible on the Commission's webpage on the evaluation of the legislative framework for tobacco control5.

The short interval between the publication of the Staff Working Document and that of the supporting study reflected the time required to complete the Commission’s internal publication process for the study.
